props.title: Amazing Grace
props.initialSlug: Anti-slavery crusader fights to end British trade

sections.content: **Amazing Grace** (2006) powerfully chronicles William Wilberforce's decades-long battle to end the British slave trade, with Ioan Gruffudd delivering a passionate performance as the tireless abolitionist. The film expertly weaves together political drama and moral conviction, similar to how **Lincoln** (2012) approached American slavery through legislative struggle. Director Michael Apted brings the same careful attention to historical detail that distinguished his work on **Glory** (1989), though here focusing on the parliamentary fight rather than armed conflict.

sections.content: Historical biopics tackling slavery and human rights gained new urgency in the 2000s and 2010s. **Belle** (2013) examined race and class in 18th century England through the true story of Dido Elizabeth Belle. **The Butler** (2013) spanned decades of American civil rights progress through one man's White House service. These films share Amazing Grace's approach of personalizing vast historical movements through intimate character studies. SUBHEAD: Political Reform Through Individual Action

Amazing Grace fits into a proud tradition of films about individuals fighting corrupt systems. Like **Milk** (2008) and **Selma** (2014), it shows how persistent activism can overcome entrenched opposition. The film's portrayal of parliamentary procedure and behind-the-scenes negotiation recalls **The Iron Lady** (2011) and **Darkest Hour** (2017), though with abolition rather than war as its moral crucible.
